description.en: Find the bank, the post office, the mosque and the shops, say where things are, and talk about places the Kenyan way.
description.so: Hel bangiga, boostada, masjidka iyo dukaamada, sheeg meesha ay wax ku yaalliin, oo meelaha uga hadal sida Kenyaanka.

body.en: Add -ni to a place to say at, in or to it: shule → shuleni (at school), duka → dukani (at the shop), kanisa → kanisani, msikiti → msikitini. With newer words like benki, posta and hospitali, Kenyans usually skip -ni: Niko benki, Naenda posta.
body.so: Meel ku dar -ni si aad u tiraahdo ku, gudaha ama u: shule → shuleni (iskuulka), duka → dukani (dukaanka), kanisa → kanisani, msikiti → msikitini. Erayada cusub sida benki, posta iyo hospitali, Kenyaanku badanaa -ni way ka tagaan: Niko benki, Naenda posta.

body.en: In Kenya you will constantly hear kwa used for places: Niko kwa duka (I'm at the shop), Tukutane kwa benki (Let's meet at the bank). The standard form is Niko dukani. Kwa with a person is standard everywhere: kwa Mama Amina means 'at Mama Amina's place'. Understand both, and use dukani when you write.
body.so: Kenya waxaad had iyo jeer maqli doontaa kwa oo loo isticmaalo meelaha: Niko kwa duka (Dukaanka ayaan joogaa), Tukutane kwa benki (Aan ku kulanno bangiga). Qaabka rasmiga ah waa Niko dukani. Kwa marka qof la raaciyo meel walba waa sax: kwa Mama Amina waxay ka dhigan tahay 'Mama Amina gurigeeda'. Labadaba faham, qoraalkana ku isticmaal dukani.

body.en: Use iko for places and things (Benki iko wapi? Where is the bank?) and yuko for people (Amina yuko wapi?). Location words are followed by ya or na: mbele ya (in front of), nyuma ya (behind), kando ya (beside), ndani ya (inside), nje ya (outside), katikati ya (between, in the middle of), karibu na (near), mbali na (far from).
body.so: Iko u isticmaal meelaha iyo waxyaabaha (Benki iko wapi? Bangigu xaggee buu ku yaal?), yuko-na dadka (Amina yuko wapi?). Erayada goobta waxaa raaca ya ama na: mbele ya (hor), nyuma ya (gadaal), kando ya (ag, dhinac), ndani ya (gudaha), nje ya (dibadda), katikati ya (dhexda), karibu na (u dhow), mbali na (ka fog).

examples.en: The post office is in front of the bank.
examples.so: Boostadu waxay ku taal bangiga hortiisa.

examples.en: The car is outside the hospital.

body.en: In standard Swahili the word for 'is (located)' agrees with the noun: shule iko, duka liko, msikiti uko, kituo kiko. In everyday Kenyan speech iko is used for almost everything, so you will often hear Msikiti iko wapi? Learn the standard form, but don't be surprised by iko.
body.so: Sawaaxiliga rasmiga ah, erayga 'wuu yaal' wuxuu la jaanqaadaa magaca: shule iko, duka liko, msikiti uko, kituo kiko. Hadalka maalinlaha ah ee Kenya iko ayaa loo isticmaalaa ku dhawaad wax walba, sidaas darteed badanaa waxaad maqli doontaa Msikiti iko wapi? Baro qaabka rasmiga ah, laakiin ha la yaabin iko.

body.en: Eastleigh in Nairobi is the centre of Somali-Kenyan business, sometimes called Little Mogadishu. Its malls and tall buildings sell clothes, fabric, electronics and gold, often at wholesale prices, and its hotelis serve Somali food. People from all over Kenya shop there, and you will hear Somali and Swahili side by side.
body.so: Eastleigh oo ku taal Nairobi waa xarunta ganacsiga Soomaali-Kenyaanka, mararka qaarna waxaa loogu yeeraa Muqdisho Yar. Moolasheeda iyo dhismayaasheeda dhaadheer waxaa lagu iibiyaa dhar, maro, qalab elektaroonig ah iyo dahab, badanaa qiimaha jumladda, hoteliyadeeduna waxay bixiyaan cunto Soomaali ah. Dad Kenya oo dhan ka yimid ayaa halkaas wax ka iibsada, waxaadna maqli doontaa Soomaali iyo Sawaaxili oo isla socda.

note.en: A university is chuo kikuu (lit. big college).
note.so: Jaamacaddu waa chuo kikuu (macnaha erayga: kulliyad weyn).
Kenyaan badan waxay iska yiraahdaan sheli.
Kenyaanku sidoo kale waxay yiraahdaan pembeni ya.

note.en: Ng'ambo means 'the other side'. On its own it often means abroad.
note.so: Ng'ambo waxay ka dhigan tahay 'dhinaca kale'. Keligeed badanaa waxay ka dhigan tahay dibadda (dal shisheeye).

note.en: duka + -ni: the standard way to say 'at the shop'.
note.so: duka + -ni: habka rasmiga ah ee lagu yiraahdo 'dukaanka'.

note.en: Very common in Kenya. Standard Swahili says Niko dukani.
note.so: Kenya aad bay ugu badan tahay. Sawaaxiliga rasmiga ah wuxuu yiraahdaa Niko dukani.

note.en: Kwa + a person means at their home or business. This is standard everywhere.
note.so: Kwa + qof waxay ka dhigan tahay gurigiisa ama meeshiisa ganacsiga. Tani meel walba waa sax.

items.en: I'm going to the post office

note.en: Standard: msikiti uko. In Nairobi you will often hear Msikiti iko wapi?
note.so: Rasmi: msikiti uko. Nairobi badanaa waxaad maqli doontaa Msikiti iko wapi?

note.en: Said to a friend, Umepotea! means 'Long time no see!'
note.so: Marka saaxiib loo yiraahdo, Umepotea! waxay ka dhigan tahay 'Waa lagu waayay!'

note.en: For a place further away or out of sight, say huko.
note.so: Meel ka sii fog ama aan la arkayn, dheh huko.

items.en: There are lots of shops in Eastleigh
items.so: Eastleigh dukaamo badan ayaa ku yaal

note.en: In everyday speech you will also hear floor ya pili. Ghorofa on its own can mean a tall building.
note.so: Hadalka maalinlaha ah sidoo kale waxaad maqli doontaa floor ya pili. Ghorofa keligeed waxay ka dhigan kartaa dhisme dheer.

items.so: Dukaanka Faarax xaggee buu ku yaal?

note.en: Duka takes liko in standard Swahili; many people just say iko.
note.so: Duka waxay qaadataa liko Sawaaxiliga rasmiga ah; dad badan waxay iska yiraahdaan iko.

items.en: It's crowded (lit. there are many people)

explain.so: 'Iskuulku ma kaniisadda horteeda ayuu ku yaal?' – 'Maya, kaniisadda gadaasheeda ayuu ku yaal.'

lines.en: I'm at the shop. I'm buying milk.
lines.so: Dukaanka ayaan joogaa. Caano ayaan iibsanayaa.
